title: the *four-minute* mobility authority plan
dek: A bounded content strategy for an 11-year physical therapist helping time-poor desk workers move consistently. It uses six frozen synthetic signals and does not invent the founder's clinical point of view.
sources: 6 synthetic YouTube rows + supplied client intake

sections.heading: the call
sections.body: Own minimum-effective mobility for desk workers: short routines that survive real work and family life. The evidence supports one opening. A four-minute mobility result ran at 6.4 times its synthetic channel baseline. The authority layer comes from the founder's supplied 11 years of practice, but the clinical lesson itself remains hers to articulate.

sections.heading: what this run can honestly support
who this is for
sections.body:
A 38-year-old product manager with two children, a standing desk they rarely use, and a back that feels fine until it suddenly does not. They have saved stretching videos before. The videos did not survive the week. They do not need more exercises; they need a small, credible routine they can keep.

The founder's supplied edge is unusually concrete: 11 years as a physical therapist and direct experience with roughly 1,000 desk-worker backs. That is authority material, not permission for the system to invent a clinical conclusion.

rows.claim: A minimum-effective mobility promise earned the only direct topic qualification
rows.evidence: The four-minute warm-up video produced 1,210,043 synthetic views, 6.4 times its channel baseline, with 5.1% engagement.

rows.claim: A proof-led practitioner format is worth transferring, not copying
rows.evidence: The receipt-confession video ran at 9.0 times baseline, but its topic targeted coaches. Only the format transfers to the founder's real clinical experience.

rows.claim: The lane is promising, not proven
rows.evidence: The sample contains one direct mobility winner and no owned conversion evidence. Three real founder-led batches are the first useful demand test.

sections.heading: the starting trio
sections.dek: Two narrow buyer lanes and one practitioner-authority lane, adapted to three founder-shot pieces per week.

items.why: The only direct topic signal. The founder must choose the movements, exclusions, and safety language.
Uses the buyer's exact intake language to turn latent worry into a qualified question; performance remains untested.
Transfers the proven receipt-confession format to a real observation from 11 years of practice; the observation itself stays human-owned.

sections.heading: what the system may and may not do

items.name: reaction questions
items.note: prompt the founder without supplying the opinion

items.title: Run the starting trio
items.body: Three founder-shot pieces per week. Observe; do not judge a piece inside 24 hours.

items.title: Make the first keep-or-revise call
items.body: Use qualified replies, saves, page visits, inquiries, and sales. Raw reach alone does not decide.

items.title: Repeat the best pair
items.body: Change either the topic or the format, never both at once.

items.title: Replace the frozen snapshot
items.body: Run a real 10–30 channel scan and see whether the four-minute opening repeats.

items.title: Build repetitions around what survived
items.body: Add volume only after the signal holds across three batches.

sections.heading: what this proves and what it doesn't
sections.body: This proves the content system can turn a thin, frozen input into a usable and honest client strategy without filling gaps with confident fiction. It does not prove current demand, clinical efficacy, conversion lift, cohort sales, or revenue. The synthetic video links are validation receipts, not live market evidence. Before production, the founder must supply the clinical observation, exercise selection, contraindications, permission-safe story, voice, and final approval.
